state:
- Exposure gate (B1) rests entirely on recalled, unverified PK/IC50 anchors (100–120 µM total, >99% binding, IC50 0.5–6 µM). A 2–3× error in any anchor flips the go/no-go, so 'administrative falsification' could kill a viable hypothesis or pass an unviable one; fix by verifying label and primary pharmacology data before applying the gate and making the measured primary-blast EC50, not recalled arithmetic, the decisive readout.
- The S2-derived dual-mechanism bridge (B3) is mechanistically weak: removing DHODH electron donation to the CoQ pool does not obviously stress OXPHOS-dependent, fatty-acid-oxidation residual cells, and S2's chemo-persistent population was not shown to depend on DHODH flux; fix by dropping B3 or testing it directly (oxygen consumption/reserve capacity in chemo-persistent cells ± DHODH inhibition) before any combination work is proposed.
- Novelty and selectivity hinge on unresolved prior art the answer defers: brequinar's 1990s AML trials (known myelosuppression) and any published leflunomide/teriflunomide-in-AML data directly threaten both the promisingness and the 20–30% normal-colony margin, since potent DHODH inhibition is expected to hit cycling normal CD34+ cells; fix by completing prior-art/label verification before scoring, and pre-specifying how the flux-based stratifier is re-scoped if published work covers it or the DHO:orotate biomarker proves assay-unstable.
